title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Packaging, and Day‑2 Ops
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document is the canonical Redwood Inference guide for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, on‑prem packaging and installer options, customer requirements, a deployment checklist, step-by-step deployment procedures for VPC and on‑prem installs, day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling), and upgrade & rollback procedures. Intended audience: SREs, platform engineers, solutions engineers, and security reviewers.

Scope and goals:
- Provide a repeatable, auditable deployment process for private customers.
- Capture network, compute, storage, and security requirements for pre-sales and engineering handoffs.
- Define day‑2 operational runbooks and escalation paths.
- Standardize upgrade and rollback processes to minimize customer downtime.

Table of contents:
1) Overview and key concepts
2) Reference architectures
3) On‑prem packaging & installer options
4) Customer requirements library (pre‑deployment checklist)
5) VPC deployment procedure (step-by-step)
6) On‑prem deployment procedure (step-by-step)
7) Day‑2 operations and runbooks
8) Upgrade and rollback procedures
9) Troubleshooting and common issues
10) Ownership, SLAs, and contacts

1) Overview and key concepts
- Redwood Private provides the same inference runtime used in hosted and dedicated environments but deployed into customer-controlled networks.
- Two supported deployment modes described here:
  * VPC deployment: Redwood control plane with customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink. Data paths and inference nodes can be placed in customer cloud accounts (AWS/Azure/GCP) depending on contract.
  * On‑prem deployment: Appliance/containerized package deployed on customer-owned hardware, air-gapped or with restricted egress as required.
- Key operational assumptions: customers provide network connectivity, certificates, and node capacity. Redwood provides an operator package and remote support (if included in contract).

2) Reference architectures
- Lightweight VPC reference (small customers, non-critical workloads):
  * 3x inference worker nodes (GPU-enabled), 2x control-plane VMs, database (managed or local) with HA, NAT gateway, and minimal egress.
  * Placement: inference nodes in private subnets, control plane in management subnet.
- Production VPC reference (enterprise/high-throughput):
  * Multi-AZ setup with autoscaling inference pools, dedicated logging and metrics cluster, dedicated KMS integration, and mirrored standby control-plane for failover.
  * Use transit gateway or PrivateLink for control-plane connectivity to Redwood management plane when required by contract.
- On‑prem reference (rack-based):
  * 2x management nodes (HA), N inference racks (each rack: 4‑8 GPU servers), shared storage (NFS or distributed block store), bastion host for maintenance, and a local KMS/HSM integration where required.

3) On‑prem packaging & installer options
- Packaging choices:
  * Distribution container images (OCI) + Helm charts for Kubernetes-based installs.
  * OVA/VM images for bare-metal virtualization environments.
  * Bare-metal installer with systemd unit files for customers not using Kubernetes.
- Installer options and recommended uses:
  * Helm charts: recommended for customers with Kubernetes (EKS/AKS/GKE/on-prem K8s). Offers easier upgrades and canary strategies.
  * OVA: good for quick proof-of-concept on VMware.
  * Bare-metal: required for strict regulatory or air-gapped environments where orchestration layers are not permitted.
- Packaging artifacts included in release bundle:
  * release.tar.gz (versioned), checksums, signed manifest, installer script, sample k8s values.yaml, example firewall/seclist rules, and integration adapters for common KMS vendors.

4) Customer requirements library (pre‑deployment checklist)
- Network (minimum):
  | Requirement                       | Details / Recommendation                             |
  | ----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
  | Public endpoints                  | If control-plane connectivity required, provide egress to Redwood management endpoints or PrivateLink setup |
  | CIDR and route tables             | Customer must share CIDR ranges and routing table configuration for peering or transit setup |
  | Required ports                    | See Ports & Protocols table below                       |

- Compute & storage:
  | Requirement                       | Minimum per node / recommended                       |
  | ----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
  | Inference GPU node                | 1x NVIDIA A10/A100-class GPU, 64GB RAM, 500GB NVMe    |
  | Control plane node                | 4vCPU, 16GB RAM, 200GB SSD                            |
  | Shared storage                    | 2x replicated volumes, 1‑2 TB depending on model cache size |

- Security & identity:
  - TLS certificates: either customer-provided CA certs or Redwood-signed certs deployed by operator.
  - KMS/HSM: configuration details, access controls, and required roles (see sample IAM policies).
  - RBAC: customer defines SRE and admin roles; Redwood recommends least-privilege for service accounts.

- Ports & Protocols (example):
  - 443 TCP: control plane API (if external)
  - 50051 TCP: internal gRPC (inference workers)
  - 9100 TCP: node exporter / metrics (monitoring)
  - 2379 TCP: etcd (if using local etcd cluster)
  - 22 TCP: optional bastion SSH for maintenance (restrict by source IP)

5) VPC deployment procedure (high-level, step-by-step)
1. Pre-deployment: Confirm customer checklist items and receive CIDR, IAM roles, and KMS access.
2. Network setup: Configure VPC peering or PrivateLink; apply route table updates and security lists.
3. Provision compute: Create control-plane instances, autoscaling group or node pools for inference, attach GPUs and disk volumes.
4. Install dependencies: Docker/container runtime, kubelet (if Kubernetes), required OS packages, and monitoring agents.
5. Deploy control plane: Apply Helm chart or run installer; verify control plane APIs respond on health endpoints.
6. Deploy inference workers: Scale up a minimal pool (3 workers) and run smoke tests using packaged test prompt set.
7. Integrations: Configure KMS, logging destinations (customer ELK/Datadog), and networking egress rules.
8. Validation: Run performance and correctness tests (latency, throughput, sample prompts), verify logs and metrics ingestion, and capture baseline dashboards.
9. Handover: Share runbooks, SLOs, and access controls with customer SREs.

6) On‑prem deployment procedure (high-level, step-by-step)
1. Pre-deployment: Confirm hardware inventory, IP allocation, DNS plan, and rack access windows.
2. Prepare infrastructure: Rack and cable servers, configure out-of-band management (iLO/DRAC/BMC), and set BIOS/firmware baselines.
3. Storage: Provision shared storage and verify performance (IOPS/latency) meets model caching requirements.
4. Install OS & dependencies: Apply hardened OS image, disable unnecessary services, install container runtime or virtualization platform.
5. Install Redwood package: Unpack release bundle, verify signatures, run installer (Helm/OVA/bare-metal).
6. Configure KMS & certificates: On‑prem KMS adapters or HSM setup; install TLS certs and validate chain.
7. Start services and validate health: Confirm control plane, model registry, and inference workers are healthy.
8. Run functional and perf validation: Run regression prompt sets, measure P95 latency and throughput for representative workloads.
9. Handover and documentation: Provide runbook, contact matrix, and maintenance windows.

7) Day‑2 operations and runbooks
- Monitoring & alerting:
  * Required dashboards: per-node GPU utilization, per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), token throughput, model cache hit rate, and error rate by code.
  * Default alerts:
    - GPU saturation > 85% for 10m -> SEV-3 alert to platform oncall
    - P95 latency > target SLO for 5m -> SEV-2, trigger autoscaling if configured
    - Control plane unhealthy -> SEV-1, follow incident response runbook
- Backups & DR:
  * Control plane DB backups: daily snapshot retained 30 days.
  * Model artifacts: maintain separate artifact repo and immutable model versions; replicate critical model weights to secondary storage.
- Scaling & capacity management:
  * Autoscaling guidance: set min/max worker counts based on baseline throughput and peak multipliers; prefer horizontal scaling for GPU pools.
  * On‑prem vertical scaling: coordinate maintenance windows for hardware upgrades; verify drivers and CUDA versions.
- Maintenance procedures:
  1. Scheduled maintenance start: notify customer SRE and record window.
  2. Drain workers: Mark nodes as unschedulable and wait for in-flight requests to finish (grace period).
  3. Apply OS/driver updates: Reboot nodes one at a time and validate health.
  4. Resume traffic and validate metrics post-maintenance.

8) Upgrade & rollback procedures
- Policy: All upgrades must be tested in an isolated staging environment that mirrors production. Use canary or blue/green strategies depending on customer risk tolerance.
- Helm/K8s upgrade (recommended):
  1. Prepare release bundle and verify signatures.
  2. Deploy canary release to 1‑2 workers or a test namespace.
  3. Run automated smoke and perf tests.
  4. Gradually roll out to remaining nodes with monitoring gates at each step.
  5. If any gate fails, execute rollback procedure.
- Bare-metal/OVA upgrade:
  * Upgrade one management node, validate, then advance to worker racks one at a time.
- Rollback procedure (general):
  1. Identify failing release and mark health checks degraded.
  2. Trigger automated rollback (helm rollback <release> <revision>) or redeploy previous OVA.
  3. Reconnect downgraded nodes to control plane, validate data compatibility, and run smoke tests.
  4. Postmortem and root cause analysis to be filed within 72 hours of rollback.

9) Troubleshooting and common issues
- High latency with low GPU utilization:
  * Check network egress rules and inter-node bandwidth. Verify NVLink and PCIe topology on single-node configs.
  * Inspect model cache hit rates; high cold-cache rates increase end-to-end latency.
- Worker crash loops after upgrade:
  * Check driver/CUDA version mismatches and container runtime logs.
  * Verify that model artifacts and config schemas are backward compatible.
- Monitoring gaps:
  * Ensure exporters are running and metrics are scraped. Check firewall rules for metrics endpoints.

10) Ownership, SLAs, and contacts
- Document ownership:
  * Engineering SRE oncall: eng-sre@redwood.example.com
  * Private Deployments PM: asha.patel@redwood.example.com
  * Solutions Engineering (customer-facing): se-team@redwood.example.com
- SLA expectations (example for Dedicated/Private customers):
  * Uptime: 99.5% for control plane (monthly), response time targets defined per contract.
  * Incident response: SEV-1 acknowledged within 15 minutes, SEV-2 within 60 minutes.
